bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /images endpoint accepts an image source and sends the resulting bytes to Sharp. For SVG input, imageProcessor deliberately rasterizes at density 300 with limitInputPixels disabled and performs no structural bound on use-element shadow-tree depth or pattern-tile dimensions. A crafted SVG can therefore make the underlying SVG renderer consume unbounded CPU or memory until the application server, and potentially the host, is denied service.
flaw_origin: Commit 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 first added packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts and its unsafe SVG branch, including density: 300 and limitInputPixels: false, plus the request handler that passes attacker-selected src into the processor. Its immediate child a839543becedb75324a16c38194eb4c64ba5f635 registered that handler as public GET /images; the first affected release v2.1.0 contains both commits. The root-cause lines themselves originate in 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143, so the later route-enablement commit is lifecycle context rather than the BIC.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 shows author and committer The Nguyen <6950941+treoden@users.noreply.github.com>, subject 'Feat: Image component', no message body, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: The GitHub advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m2q5-xhqg-92r2 and the researcher analysis https://pages.dos-m0nk3y.com/blog/EverShop%202.1.0%20-%20Unauthenticated%20DoS/ identify public GET /images and the Sharp SVG branch as the DoS path, list <=2.1.0 as affected, and list no patched version. git show 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 -- packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts shows the new isSvg check and sharp(sourceImageBuffer, { density: 300, limitInputPixels: false }).resize(...), followed by encoding/toBuffer work; the same commit also newly adds the handler that accepts query src/w/h and calls imageProcessor. git blame -L on the SVG-special-handling block at v2.1.0 attributes every relevant line (release lines 287-297, including limitInputPixels: false at line 294) to 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143. git log -S 'limitInputPixels: false' --all finds only that addition. Direct parent-tree verification with git ls-tree -r 753e8aeac5e7a9753731a8ad0f449c05cb2fa61e returns no handler, route, or imageProcessor path, while git ls-tree -r 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 shows the new handler and processor blobs. Commit a839543becedb75324a16c38194eb4c64ba5f635, whose parent is the BIC, adds route.json with methods GET and path /images. Version checking shows v2.0.1 has none of the handler/route/processor paths, whereas v2.1.0 contains all three and git tag --contains the BIC includes v2.1.0. No direct resource-bound fix exists in reachable history: git log --all --follow for imageProcessor has no SVG-safety change, and git grep at v2.1.0, v2.1.1, v2.1.2, and v2.2.1 still finds limitInputPixels: false. Commit af6e6fd935c4194668b11a924b847542598941f7, released in v2.2.1, replaces arbitrary fetch with an external-host allowlist for the separate SSRF path, but does not validate or bound SVG rendering and is therefore not recorded as this CVE's fix. The advisory continues to report patched versions: None.
reasoning: The vulnerable mechanism is the unbounded SVG rasterization policy, not merely Sharp usage or the later route file. History was therefore traced from the advisory-named branch: 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 is the smallest commit that first wrote the unsafe SVG configuration and the handler-to-processor flow; a839543becedb75324a16c38194eb4c64ba5f635 only makes the already-written flow reachable at GET /images. The exact BIC parent tree lacks both relevant source files, directly proving parent absence. The v2.0.1/v2.1.0 tree boundary proves the feature first enters the advisory's affected release line. Later SSRF allowlisting narrows one way an unauthenticated caller can supply remote bytes but leaves the advisory's root cause, including limitInputPixels: false and absence of SVG structural limits, intact, so no fix SHA or patched boundary can honestly be assigned. Finally, attribution is limited to the BIC commit object as required: it has a human author/committer and no AI marker or trailer. The correct closed causal verdict is therefore NOT_AI despite the vulnerability remaining unpatched.
remaining_gap: The vulnerability is genuinely unpatched in reachable repository history: neither a direct SVG structural-limit fix nor an official patched version exists, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are null. The v2.2.1 SSRF allowlist is only an attack-source mitigation and does not remove the unsafe SVG-processing mechanism.
